messages:
Aisha: quick heads up — after yesterday's rollout p95 for gen with seq=1024 jumped ~18%.
Aisha: grabbed an nsys trace of a hot request, timeline looks dominated by a single kernel we didn't expect: `wf_merge_loop_v3`.
Tom: ouch. can you paste the nsys command you used?
Aisha: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=wf_v3_1024 ./run_infer --seq_len 1024 --batch 4`
Aisha: top-line from the summary (nsys / perf summary):
Aisha: ```
Top kernels by GPU time:
1) wf_merge_loop_v3        42.3%   avg_time 6.2ms   sm_util 31.8%  occupancy 72%
2) kv_prefetch_coalesce    18.6%   avg_time 2.7ms   sm_util 55.2%  occupancy 84%
3) attn_fwd_fused          12.1%   avg_time 1.8ms   sm_util 78.9%  occupancy 95%
``` 
Aisha: note wf_merge_loop_v3 is high time but low sm_util vs attn_fwd_fused which is efficient — smells like warp stalls or memory serialization.
Tom: low sm_util + decent occupancy -> warp_serialize / memory dependency or long-running divergent branches.
Tom: can you capture stall reasons? `nvprof --metrics warp_efficiency,elapsed_cycles_sm,dram__throughput` or use `nsys convert --report` to get CU stall breakdown.
perf-bot: perf summary (automated): wf_merge_loop_v3 shows high `issue_stalled` and `mem_barrier` samples, increased since commit 9f3a7c (merge coalescer change)
Kai: that commit switched the merge path to a block-global cooperative loop that uses atomics for per-wave counters — could be contention at high seq lengths when many KV hits cause early exits.
Kai: hypothesize: merge path has a hot atomic on `global_merge_cursor`. At small seq it is fine, at long seq many threads spin waiting -> WARPS stall.
Egor: I can repro locally with a micro-bench. Quick test: toggle the merge path off -> regression disappears. So it's definitely the new path.
Tom: next diagnostics:
Tom: 1) capture `nvprof --analysis-metrics` for `sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_active.avg.pct` and `sm__thread_inst_executed.avg`;
Tom: 2) run traces at seq=[64,256,1024] and batch=[1,4,8] to see breakpoints;
Tom: 3) add NVTX markers around the merge loop to isolate GPU timeline.
Aisha: added NVTX in a dev build; re-ran with batch=4 seq=1024 -> timeline shows long contiguous blocks of `wf_merge_loop_v3` with periodic small kv_prefetch spikes.
Aisha: flame excerpt (ascii):
Aisha: `|-- wf_merge_loop_v3 [6.2ms]
Aisha:     |-- warp_wait (spin) [3.1ms]
Aisha:     |-- global_loads [1.6ms]
Aisha:     |-- atomic_cas_loop [1.3ms]`
Kai: warp_wait + atomic_cas_loop = classic synchronization backpressure. We should consider per-block private counters (reduce atomics) or switch to warp-level ballot+prefix sum.
Egor: micro-bench results:
Egor: seq=1024 batch=4: wf_merge_loop_v3 avg 6.1ms
Egor: seq=256 batch=4: wf_merge_loop_v3 avg 1.4ms
Egor: seq=64 batch=4: wf_merge_loop_v3 avg 0.3ms
Egor: so the cost scales superlinearly with seq length -> more opportunities to spin.
Tom: mitigation ideas (quick wins):
Tom: - short-term: fall back to old merge path for seq>512 or detected skewed KV hitrate
Tom: - medium-term: rework to per-warp cooperative aggregation using ballot/prefix to avoid global atomics
Tom: - perf tweak: tune block size/threads-per-block to reduce idle lanes (try 128->256 threads/blk)
Aisha: agree fallback looks lowest-risk for release rollback. We can gate with feature flag + telemetry.
Kai: I'll prototype a warp-level aggregator this week and run nvprof to compare `issue_stalled` and `warp_efficiency`.
perf-bot: action created: PERF-4325 assign Kai owner, ETA 3d; fallback flag task assigned to Egor.
Egor: I'll add the feature flag and a small e2e canary in staging. Also will capture nvprof metrics before/after for the changelist.
Aisha: TL;DR: root cause = merge-path global atomic contention -> causes `wf_merge_loop_v3` to dominate GPU time with high stall samples at high seq lengths. Short-term: fallback gate. Medium-term: per-warp non-atomic aggregator.
Tom: nice triage. Please paste updated nvprof/ nsight summaries when available. :thumbsup:
Kai: will do. ping me if you want the micro-bench harness (has scripts to sweep seq/batch/hitrate).
